children: Arabica coffee futures fell to a 10-week low on Thursday, weighed partly by a favourable outlook for next year's crop in top producer Brazil, while sugar prices rose.
fell 2.65% to $2.8430 per lb by 1010 GMT, after setting a 10-week low of $2.8355.
* Dealers said this year's harvest in Brazil is now nearly complete and the focus was on switching to the 2027 crop.
* Exchange certified stocks have now edged above a recent 26-year low, boosted by some additional supplies from Brazil, they said.
* Exchange stocks stood at 220,452 bags as of September 9, up from 218,838 bags a day earlier. At the same time last year, stocks stood at 685,945 bags, dealers noted.
* There were also 54,310 bags from Brazil and 960 bags from Kenya pending grading.
rose 1.5% to 18.67 cents per lb, climbing back towards last week's 16-month high of 18.77 cents.
* Dealers said the run-up has been driven by tight supplies in top consumer India and the current strength of energy markets, which could encourage more use of cane to make biofuel ethanol.

* The Indian government has asked sugar mills to ensure adequate supplies during the festival season, with domestic mills seeking to import nearly 800,000 tons of duty-free raw sugar, an official from the food ministry said on Thursday.

* Dealers noted September (LCCU6) was trading at a discount of around £200 to December in the run-up to its expiry on September 15, indicating little appetite to take delivery of cocoa against the contract.
